findings.title: A shard-aware connection rejected as excess is still dropped without decrementing…
findings.claim: A shard-aware connection rejected as excess is still dropped without decrementing total_connections, so the metric stays unbalanced on a discard path that sits right next to the ones this PR fixed.

findings.title: When the pool worker stops, its pooled, excess and in-flight connections are dropped…
findings.claim: When the pool worker stops, its pooled, excess and in-flight connections are dropped without decrementing total_connections. The 'balance metrics when clearing pools' change does not cover this teardown.

findings.title: The keyspace-setup future still has no timeout, so a USE request that hangs keeps the…
findings.claim: The keyspace-setup future still has no timeout, so a USE request that hangs keeps the connection in ready_connections indefinitely. That leaves is_filling() true and blocks both refills and the new failure-reporting path.

findings.title: The keyspace setup failure is now logged at debug
findings.claim: The keyspace setup failure is now logged at debug! rather than warn!, which removes the only operator-visible signal for this failure.

findings.title: The test keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill builds an event state that production…
findings.claim: The test keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill builds an event state that production never produces: a Keyspace error with keyspace_name None and a shard-aware requested_shard. It also never checks that a refill actually happens.

findings.title: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state awaits ready_connections
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state awaits ready_connections.next() with no timeout, and the USE path it waits on has no client-side timeout either.

findings.title: The two new keyspace tests do not call setup_tracing(), even though CONTRIBUTING…
findings.claim: The two new keyspace tests do not call setup_tracing(), even though CONTRIBUTING requires new tests to call it. The other new tests in this PR do.

findings.title: Both keyspace tests copy PoolRefiller construction inline (endpoint, notifiers, metrics,…
findings.claim: Both keyspace tests copy PoolRefiller construction inline (endpoint, notifiers, metrics, reconnect policy) instead of reusing or extending the existing mock_pool_refiller helper.

findings.title: All four commits have a subject line only
findings.claim: All four commits have a subject line only. None explains what changed or why, and there is no PR description, which the repository's contribution rules require.

findings.title: None of the four commits has a message body
findings.claim: None of the four commits has a message body. Each is just a subject line, so none explains why the change was made. This violates a documented rule.

findings.title: The metrics fix is incomplete (shotgun surgery)
findings.claim: The metrics fix is incomplete (shotgun surgery). Each clear site needs its own hand-added `decrement_total_connections(...)`, and one path that drops an already-counted connection still has none: the rejected shard-aware connection branch.

findings.title: The same 'decrement N, then clear excess_connections' sequence appears at three sites
findings.claim: The same 'decrement N, then clear excess_connections' sequence appears at three sites. In maybe_reshard the decrement is computed 8 lines before the clears it accounts for, so it depends on statement order.

findings.title: `decrement_total_connections` makes N separate atomic fetch_sub calls in a loop
findings.claim: `decrement_total_connections` makes N separate atomic fetch_sub calls in a loop. A batch decrement belongs on Metrics, next to inc_total_connections and dec_total_connections.

findings.title: The new private enum `ConnectionSetupError` is easy to confuse with the existing public…
findings.claim: The new private enum `ConnectionSetupError` is easy to confuse with the existing public `ConnectionSetupRequestError` and `ConnectionError::ConnectionSetupRequestError`. Its `Connection` variant wraps any connection error, not just setup failures.

findings.title: The new Keyspace arm copies the Connection arm's logic: set had_error_since_last_refill,…
findings.claim: The new Keyspace arm copies the Connection arm's logic: set had_error_since_last_refill, then report the error if `!is_filling() && is_empty()`. There are now two copies of the 'report when the last attempt failed' rule.

findings.title: Commit 7f48315d adds public API: a `ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError` variant and a…
findings.claim: Commit 7f48315d adds public API: a `ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError` variant and a public `From<UseKeyspaceError> for ConnectionError`. The commit does not mention it, and the variant doesn't fit the documented meaning of ConnectionError.

findings.title: The name `keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill` claims more than the test checks
findings.claim: The name `keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill` claims more than the test checks. It never runs the refiller loop and never sees a refill happen; it only checks state flags and the `need_filling()` predicate.

findings.title: `keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state` re-implements the proxy setup and the…
findings.claim: `keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state` re-implements the proxy setup and the OPTIONS/STARTUP rules from `start_simulated_node`. The resharding metrics test also pastes the same rule vectors inline twice.

findings.title: `unrequested_connection_event` is gated on `#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]` but has nothing…
findings.claim: `unrequested_connection_event` is gated on `#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]` but has nothing to do with metrics, so the ungated keyspace test writes the same code out inline three times.

findings.title: The forged SetKeyspace response hard-codes the keyspace name "keyspace" inside a raw…
findings.claim: The forged SetKeyspace response hard-codes the keyspace name "keyspace" inside a raw byte literal. It ignores the keyspace actually requested and has to match a separate string literal used for current_keyspace.

findings.title: Commit 617139df's subject, 'avoid busy-waiting', overstates the change
findings.claim: Commit 617139df's subject, 'avoid busy-waiting', overstates the change. The test still polls the metric in a loop (now sleeping 1 ms between checks) under a 5 s wall-clock timeout, and `.unwrap()` turns a timeout into an uninformative `Elapsed` panic.

findings.title: The commit subjects start with 'connection:', but the commits only touch connection_pool
findings.claim: The commit subjects start with 'connection:', but the commits only touch connection_pool.rs and errors.rs. Recent history uses 'connection_pool:' or 'Connection pool:' for pool changes.

findings.title: `keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state` shuts down in the opposite order from its…
findings.claim: `keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state` shuts down in the opposite order from its sibling tests: it calls proxy.finish() before drop(refiller). Because of that it must explicitly allow `WorkerError::DriverDisconnected`, while the siblings simply ignore the result with `let _ = proxy.finish().await`.

findings.title: The two error arms of handle_ready_connection format their errors differently: the…
findings.claim: The two error arms of handle_ready_connection format their errors differently: the Connection arm uses `{:?}` and the new Keyspace arm uses `{}`.

findings.title: A failed USE now permanently prevents the pool from accepting any new connection when…
findings.claim: A failed USE now permanently prevents the pool from accepting any new connection when the keyspace itself is unusable, such as after it is dropped. Before this PR, the connection was kept with a warning.

findings.title: Resharding and the shard-aware port update now wait for a USE request that has no…
findings.claim: Resharding and the shard-aware port update now wait for a USE request that has no timeout, so the sharder and port stay stale for as long as that USE hangs.

findings.title: The metric assertions in the keyspace tests, and all three metrics-balance tests, are…
findings.claim: The metric assertions in the keyspace tests, and all three metrics-balance tests, are compiled out under the validation the PR reports.

findings.title: The test keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill never shows that a refill is scheduled
findings.claim: The test keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill never shows that a refill is scheduled. It feeds an error that the production path cannot produce.

findings.title: The metrics behaviour change and its regression tests landed in separate commits, and…
findings.claim: The metrics behaviour change and its regression tests landed in separate commits, and neither commit message explains why.

findings.title: A USE that fails after current_keyspace has changed again discards a connection that…
findings.claim: A USE that fails after current_keyspace has changed again discards a connection that could have been retried with the new keyspace.

findings.title: The new ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError Display wording differs from every sibling…
findings.claim: The new ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError Display wording differs from every sibling `UseKeyspaceError(#[from] UseKeyspaceError)` variant in the crate. ExecutionError, PagerExecutionError and NewSessionError all use "'USE KEYSPACE <>' request failed: {0}"; the new variant uses "Failed to set keyspace while initializing a connection: {0}".

findings.title: The PR body describes only the keyspace-setup change
findings.claim: The PR body describes only the keyspace-setup change. It omits the behavior-changing metrics commit de164845 (total_connections decrements on reshard, excess-limit clearing and full-pool clearing) and its tests (0d91aa54, 617139df).

findings.title: The new public `ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError` variant's message hard-codes 'while…
findings.claim: The new public `ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError` variant's message hard-codes 'while initializing a connection', but `#[from]` makes it the target of any `?` on UseKeyspaceError inside ConnectionError-returning code, and its message format diverges from the three existing UseKeyspaceError variants.

findings.title: New helper `unrequested_connection_event` duplicates the existing…
findings.claim: New helper `unrequested_connection_event` duplicates the existing `shard_aware_attempt_result` helper body except for requested_shard, is gated on feature="metrics" though it has nothing metrics-specific, and lacks the doc comment its sibling has.

findings.title: `full_pool_clears_excess_connections_and_balances_metrics` still polls the metric in a 1…
findings.claim: `full_pool_clears_excess_connections_and_balances_metrics` still polls the metric in a 1 ms sleep loop despite the commit 'avoid busy-waiting in metrics test', and it waits on a metric value rather than on the event that clears excess connections.

findings.title: Proxy shutdown handling is inconsistent across the new tests: the keyspace test asserts…
findings.claim: Proxy shutdown handling is inconsistent across the new tests: the keyspace test asserts finish() succeeds or only reports DriverDisconnected, while the three metrics tests discard the result with `let _ =`.

findings.title: A keyspace failure on an empty pool goes through update_shared_conns(Some(err
findings.claim: A keyspace failure on an empty pool goes through update_shared_conns(Some(err.into())). That moves the pool from Initializing or Ready to Broken and emits ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost, so a keyspace-level error is reported as lost host connectivity.

findings.title: The advanced-shard-awareness mismatch check (block_advanced_shard_awareness) now waits…
findings.claim: The advanced-shard-awareness mismatch check (block_advanced_shard_awareness) now waits for USE to succeed. When USE fails, a wrong-shard advanced connection is never detected, so advanced shard awareness is not blocked.

findings.title: A broken connection during USE (UseKeyspaceError::RequestError(BrokenConnectionError))…
findings.claim: A broken connection during USE (UseKeyspaceError::RequestError(BrokenConnectionError)) is now reported as a keyspace setup failure. It increases backoff and is published as ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError instead of BrokenConnection. Sibling code in use_keyspace_result treats broken connections as non-keyspace errors.

findings.title: The new #[from] UseKeyspaceError on the public ConnectionError adds a public…
findings.claim: The new #[from] UseKeyspaceError on the public ConnectionError adds a public From<UseKeyspaceError> for ConnectionError. As a result, pool keyspace failures reach callers as ExecutionError::ConnectionPoolError(Broken{UseKeyspaceError}), not through the existing ExecutionError::UseKeyspaceError family.
